options.content:
## Demonstration: predictive scaling on live synthetic diurnal traffic

**What this shows.** Two workloads receive the same generated request program at the same time. **Target A** (left) is on the forecast path. **Target B** (right) is the reactive reference: the same operator and policy on identical traffic, without a predictive extra. Each row follows one step of the chain: demand, forecast and trust, scale decision, Ready capacity, service quality.

**What it is not.** The traffic is **synthetic**: a generated daily program, not real business demand. This is a demonstration of a running system, **not a comparison result**. Nothing on this page is a scored or qualified outcome.

**How to read the Scaling row.** The *recommendation* is what the operator calculated. *Applied scale* is the Deployment's `spec.replicas`. *Ready* is the pods that can serve. In Recommend mode the operator writes nothing, so applied scale does not follow the recommendation. *Ready capacity* is Ready replicas times the **Capacity per replica** variable at the top (set it to the autoscalers' `capacityPerReplica`, in requests per second; 0 hides the line). Around a rise in demand, compare when each target's Ready capacity rises, then check in the Forecast row whether the forecast was trusted at that time, and in the Mode and safety row whether a forecast took part in the decision. The vertical markers are the operator's scale-up writes, one colour per target.

**Reading the panels.** Each pair (A left, B right) has the same time axis, and each panel also loads the other target's series, undrawn, so that both y-axes cover the same range. A panel titled *proxy* stands in for a quantity that no metric exports yet. Not shown, because no metric exists: the autoscaler's mode, the selected forecast family, the reason for a trust change, the forecast window and lead, the requested (as opposed to applied) scale, and the qualification basis with its expiry. `kubectl describe pa` and the forecasting service's `/health` show those. The Demand and Service quality rows read the evaluation fixture's ingress, the fixture pods and the k6 generator (`deploy/eval-c28`); they stay empty for other workloads.

panels.title: A · $target_a · Demand: scheduled, received, failed
panels.description: Requests per minute for this target. Scheduled arrivals are the generator's own count: every scheduled arrival ends as a completed request or a dropped iteration, and a completed request is counted when it ends (up to the 2 s timeout after it was sent). Received is the arrival count at the ingress, the signal the autoscaler's query reads. The operator's measured rate is the value its last decision used. Failed is every ingress response outside 2xx/3xx; no ready endpoint is the part refused because no pod was Ready.

panels.title: B · $target_b · Demand: scheduled, received, failed
panels.description: Requests per minute for this target. Scheduled arrivals are the generator's own count: every scheduled arrival ends as a completed request or a dropped iteration, and a completed request is counted when it ends (up to the 2 s timeout after it was sent). Received is the arrival count at the ingress, the signal the autoscaler's query reads. The operator's measured rate is the value its last decision used. Failed is every ingress response outside 2xx/3xx; no ready endpoint is the part refused because no pod was Ready.

panels.title: A · $target_a · Forecast upper bound against demand
panels.description: The forecast upper bound of the request-rate peak in the lead window, against the measured demand (requests per minute). The operator's line is present only while a verified, eligible forecast is used in the decision. The forecaster's lines are its own latest committed bound and point maximum for every candidate family, trusted or not; the forecasting service declares these two series but does not publish values for them yet, so they stay empty until it does. The forecast window and lead are not exported as metrics.

panels.title: A · $target_a · Trust state over time
panels.description: First row: the trust phase the forecasting service reported with the last forecast, as the operator received it (Collecting, Calibrating, Shadow, Trusted, Degraded); empty while there is no forecast. Other rows: whether each candidate family's evidence gates pass, from the forecasting service. Trusted means ready to activate: Recommend mode still makes no writes. The reason for a promotion or demotion and the selected family are not exported as metrics.

panels.description: From the forecasting service, per candidate family. Coverage: the share of matured windows whose realised peak stayed at or under the issued bound over 7 days, against the configured target. Outcome availability: the share of the last day's due windows that were scored. Both are absent, not 0 or 100 %, while nothing has matured.

panels.title: A · $target_a · Conditions and decision basis
panels.description: The autoscaler's status conditions over time. ScalingActive=True means Active mode with writes permitted; False covers Recommend mode and every hold (the mode and the reason are not exported as metrics). PredictionReady=True means the operator verified a forecast as eligible now. Decision basis: 'forecast took part' while ForecastAvailable is True, otherwise 'reactive only', which is the fallback to the measured rate. TelemetryAvailable=False holds the replica count. ConflictDetected=True and ScaleOutBlocked=True are problems. The qualification basis and its expiry are not exported as metrics.

targets.expr: sum by (type) (predictive_autoscaler_condition{job="${installation}-operator-metrics", pa_install_namespace="$install_namespace", namespace="$namespace", autoscaler="$target_a", type=~"ScalingActive|PredictionReady|ForecastAvailable|TelemetryAvailable|ConflictDetected|ScaleOutBlocked", status="True"}) + 2 * sum by (type) (predictive_autoscaler_condition{job="${installation}-operator-metrics", pa_install_namespace="$install_namespace", namespace="$namespace", autoscaler="$target_a", type=~"ScalingActive|PredictionReady|ForecastAvailable|TelemetryAvailable|ConflictDetected|ScaleOutBlocked", status="Unknown"})

panels.title: B · $target_b · Conditions and decision basis
panels.description: The autoscaler's status conditions over time. ConflictDetected=True and ScaleOutBlocked=True are problems. The qualification basis and its expiry are not exported as metrics.

targets.expr: sum by (type) (predictive_autoscaler_condition{job="${installation}-operator-metrics", pa_install_namespace="$install_namespace", namespace="$namespace", autoscaler="$target_b", type=~"ScalingActive|PredictionReady|ForecastAvailable|TelemetryAvailable|ConflictDetected|ScaleOutBlocked", status="True"}) + 2 * sum by (type) (predictive_autoscaler_condition{job="${installation}-operator-metrics", pa_install_namespace="$install_namespace", namespace="$namespace", autoscaler="$target_b", type=~"ScalingActive|PredictionReady|ForecastAvailable|TelemetryAvailable|ConflictDetected|ScaleOutBlocked", status="Unknown"})

panels.title: Forecaster Ready (proxy for journal health)
panels.description: PROXY. No metric exports the forecast journal's health. The forecasting service's readiness probe fails while its journal cannot support issuance, so its Ready replica count (kube-state-metrics) stands in; a pod that is not Ready for another reason looks the same.

panels.title: Forecast state volume used (proxy for journal size)
panels.description: PROXY. No metric exports the journal's size. This is the kubelet's used and total bytes of the chart's forecast state volume (the claim <installation>-forecast-state), which holds the journal. Empty with another claim name or a volume type the kubelet does not report.

panels.title: Forecast issuances per minute
panels.description: Unique committed forecast issuances per minute, per target and candidate family (retries excluded). One issuance is expected per decision interval; a lower rate is a missed forecast opportunity.

panels.title: Forecast evidence age
panels.description: Seconds since the last prospective outcome that counts for the trust gates, per target and candidate family. Absent while there is none.

panels.title: Operator reconciles and errors per minute
panels.description: The operator's reconciles by result and its reconcile errors, per minute (controller-runtime's own metrics, all autoscalers of this installation).

panels.title: Scrape targets
panels.description: Whether the metrics store reaches the operator and the forecasting service (1 = up).
